title: Operatorless Terraform bootstrapping for Private EKS control plane with active health probes
creator: Maya Chen
description: Deliver a Terraform module and accompanying CI pipeline that can bootstrap a Redwood Private EKS control plane in a customer VPC without relying on in-cluster operators. The module must be idempotent, support safe rolling upgrades of control-plane components, expose actionable health probes (API server, controller-manager, etcd endpoints where applicable), and integrate with our drift-detection runner. This work is intended for regulated customer environments where operator installation is restricted.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module provisions EKS control plane and required IAM/KMS/networking idempotently across repeated apply cycles
Module emits and registers health-check endpoints in the RT Observability stack (prometheus job + alert rules) for API server latency, etcd quorum changes, and kube-controller-manager errors
Automated canary upgrade workflow implemented in CI that performs a rolling update with post-checks and rollback on failures
Module supports a 'dry-run' plan verification mode which fails fast on non-idempotent changes
Drift-detection job can reconcile or surface drift with clear remediation steps
Documentation and README with usage examples, variables, outputs, and migration notes included
Security review sign-off obtained for KMS integration and IAM role assumptions
updates: 2025-02-14: Ticket created — proposal and scope outlined; initial module scaffold committed to private repo (v0.1.0).

2025-02-20: Implemented idempotency hooks: resource lifecycle meta configured; discovered Terraform provider concurrency issue with aws_eks_addon causing recreate behavior — investigating provider pin.

2025-02-24: Added health probe design doc link (drive.redwood/internal/doc/priv-eks-health-probes). Decision: emit Prometheus serviceMonitor resources into observability namespace via IaC rather than operator.
2025-02-27: CI canary pipeline POC passes against dev VPC; observed intermittent etcd leader flaps during small-scale upgrades — adding forced drain wait and API-server probe backoff.
2025-03-01: Security review kickoff scheduled; KMS key policy review raised one action item to limit cross-account key usage; awaiting updated policy from Security.
notes: Avoid installing any new in-cluster operators during bootstrap to satisfy air-gapped customer requirements. For controller-like behavior (e.g., reconcilers) rely on external automation (Terraform + CI) and sidecar monitoring. Ensure module variables default to conservative settings (no automatic deletion, guarded destruction patterns). Include migration helper scripts for customers moving from atlas-provisioner.
